corrections.claimed_speedup: With emcc -O3: JS graphlib 61.1135 ms vs WASM boost::graph 10.1569 ms per Floyd-Warshall run (V=100, E=500), about 6.0x faster (derived from page data); unoptimised wasm: JS 62.16 ms vs WASM 1235.41 ms (about 20x slower, derived from page data). Priority-queue test at -O3 (300,000 elements, wasm slower throughout): inserts WASM 58.44 ms (bulk 51.99 ms) vs FastPriorityQueue.js 9.86 ms and Heap.js 13.42 ms (wasm 4-6x slower, derived from page data); peek+pop WASM 39.93 ms (bulk 33.07 ms) vs FastPriorityQueue.js 27.37 ms and Heap.js 32.31 ms.
corrections.caveats: 2017 repo (10 commits, April 22 to May 7 2017), single representative run pasted into the README, no CPU, browser or emsdk version, no licence file. Mixed result: the Floyd-Warshall win appears only at -O3, and the std::priority_queue test shows wasm slower than both JS heaps even when the loop runs entirely inside wasm (bulkInsert/bulkPops). The -O0 to -O3 gap is about 122x (1235.41 ms to 10.16 ms, derived from page data), roughly two orders of magnitude; the README's 'improved by 3 orders of magnitude' overstates it. Both timed regions include graph construction (graphlib setNode/setEdge in JS, 500 cwrap addEdge calls into wasm) and a result scan, so the harness is symmetric, but the JS baseline is a generic string-keyed object graph library, not an equivalent data layout to Boost's adjacency_list plus multi_array distance matrix. main.cpp also has a native C++ timing path (non-wasm) with no published numbers. The live benchmark pages are on azeemba.github.io (not opened; host blocked here).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: AssemblyScript ^0.28.20 (package.json devDependency): `asc 2-wasm/assembly/index.ts --outFile 2-wasm/build/sim.wasm --optimize --runtime stub --noAssert --enable simd`. Rust: cargo --release for wasm32-unknown-unknown with opt-level 3, lto, codegen-units 1, panic abort (2-wasm-rust/sim/Cargo.toml) and -C target-feature=+simd128 (.cargo/config.toml). Compiled .wasm files are checked in. Browser and JS engine not stated.
corrections.caveats: One-commit repository (2026-10-09) with a results table pasted into the README and no licence file; readings are requestAnimationFrame frame rates (capped at 60) averaged over the last 30 frames, not controlled timings, and include a WebGL upload and draw of up to 1M points shared by all CPU variants (the HUD also shows per-step sim ms, but those are not reported). The kernels are equivalent (same attractor maths over Float32Array data), but JS runs scalar f64 arithmetic while AssemblyScript runs 4-wide f32x4 SIMD, so the gap is mostly SIMD. The AssemblyScript row is internally inconsistent: 40 fps at 1M and 37 fps at 4M for four times the work, then 6 fps at 16M, so the 1M reading looks limited by something other than the simulation step. Browser, chip model and asc patch version are not stated (on a Mac the browser could be Safari's JavaScriptCore rather than V8); the JS 16M cell is blank. Counter-evidence from the same table: at 1M particles the AssemblyScript build is only 1.2x the JS loop, and Rust's wasm beats AssemblyScript at every size. No benchmark harness beyond the interactive pages; the overview page only stores each viewer's own readings in localStorage.

notes: README numbers match the record; asc flags are in package.json (the record said they were not shown).
